consensus.executive_summary: Analysis of 6 LLM quantization papers reveals widespread consensus that 4-bit weight quantization preserves standard short-context benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8k) within 0.8 points of FP16. However, a major empirical conflict exists regarding long-context deployment: 4-bit models lose up to 7.9 points at 32k context on complex reasoning tasks (Okonkwo 2024). Calibration set diversity and activation outlier protection (AWQ) are critical mediators of accuracy.
agreed_findings: Short-context instruction following is well preserved in 4-bit weight-only quantization (Zheng 2024, Schneider 2025).
Activation outlier protection (AWQ) prevents numerical collapse in low-bit representations (Okonkwo 2024, Gupta 2025).

top_contradictions.headline: Deployment safety dispute: Zheng (2024) reports 4-bit models match FP16 within 0.8 points, but Okonkwo (2024) shows a 7.9-point drop at 32k context.

recommended_next_steps: Standardize long-context (>16k) evaluations for all low-bit model releases.
Benchmark multilingual calibration sets to avoid regional language degradation.
Combine 4-bit weight compression with 4-bit KV cache kernels for end-to-end evaluation.
